Annotation.String: The `Policy` schema contains a definition for a policy.
This resource shall be used to represent a policy for a Redfish implementation.
Any writable properties can be updated.
Policies can be deleted.
All subordinate conditions trigger for this condition to trigger.

This value shall indicate that this condition requires all conditions in the `SubordinateConditions` property to evaluate to true at the same time before this condition triggers. This condition shall contain the `SubordinateConditions` property. All other properties in this condition shall be omitted.
Any subordinate conditions trigger for this condition to trigger.

This value shall indicate that this condition requires any condition in the `SubordinateConditions` property to evaluate to true before this condition triggers. This condition shall contain the `SubordinateConditions` property. All other properties in this condition shall be omitted.
Compare a value from a Redfish resource to a specified value.

This value shall indicate that the `Resource` and `Property` values are used to determine the data to read and compare to the `Value` property. This condition shall not contain the `SubordinateConditions` property.
Read a value from a Redfish resource. This condition type is used to provide values to a parent condition.

This value shall indicate that the `Resource` and `Property` values to determine the data to read. This condition shall not contain the `SubordinateConditions` and `Value` properties. This condition shall be subordinate to another condition.
Add the values of all subordinate conditions together and compare the sum to the specified value.

This value shall indicate that the values specified by each member of `SubordinateConditions` are added, and then compared using the `Operator` and `Value` properties. This condition shall not contain the `Property` or `Resource` properties. If the result of the subordinate conditions cannot be converted to a number then the value for that condition shall be `0`.
Average the values of all subordinate conditions together and compare the average to the given value.

This value shall indicate that the values specified by each member of `SubordinateConditions` are averaged, by performing an arithmetic mean, and then compared using the `Operator` and `Value` properties. This condition shall not contain the `Property` or `Resource` properties. If the result of the subordinate conditions cannot be converted to a number then the value for that condition shall be `0`.
The condition triggers when the message specified is emitted by the service.

This value shall indicate that the condition evaluates to true when the message specified in the `Value` property is emitted by the service. If the `Resource` property is specified and is not an empty string, then the condition shall only evaluate to true if the event was emitted with the resource referenced by `OriginOfCondition`. If the `MessageId` specified by the `Value` property does not specify the version of the message, then it shall apply to all versions of the message.
The response reevaluates and, if the condition is no longer true, the response actions stop at this point.

This value shall indicate that the response causes the policy condition to be reevaluated. If the condition is still true after this reevaluation, then the response actions shall continue. If the condition is no longer true, then the response actions shall stop at this point.
The response sends an event corresponding to the event parameters specified.
This value shall indicate that the response sends the event specified by the parameters in the `Event` property of the response.
The response performs a `Reset` action on the specified resource.
This value shall indicate that the response performs a `Reset` action on the resource specified by the `Resource` property with the specified `ResetType`.
The response performs an HTTP/HTTPS operation as specified by the parameters.
This value shall indicate that the response performs an HTTP/HTTPS operation as specified by the `HTTP` property.
The response performs an OEM-defined operation as specified by the parameters.
This value shall indicate that the response performs an OEM-defined operation as specified by the `Oem` property.
An indication of whether the policy is predefined by Redfish or an OEM rather than a client-defined policy.

This property shall indicate whether the policy is predefined by Redfish or an OEM as contrasted with a client-defined policy. If this property is not present, the value should be assumed to be `false`.
An indication of whether the policy is enabled.

This property indicate whether the policy is enabled. The value `true` shall indicate the service performs the actions specified by this policy. The value `false` shall indicate the service takes no actions specified by this policy.
The condition that causes the service to perform the actions of this policy.
This property shall contain the condition that causes the service to perform the actions of this policy.
A list of responses to perform when the condition is triggered.
This property shall contain a list of responses to perform when the policy condition is triggered. Services shall perform the responses sequentially.
The links to other resources that are related to this resource.
This property shall contain links to resources that are related to but are not contained by, or subordinate to, this resource.
The available actions for this resource.
This property shall contain the available actions for this resource.
The links to other resources that are related to this resource.
This Redfish Specification-described type shall contain links to resources that are related to but are not contained by, or subordinate to, this resource.
The available actions for this resource.
This type shall contain the available actions for this resource.
The available OEM-specific actions for this resource.
This property shall contain the available OEM-specific actions for this resource.
The available OEM-specific actions for this resource.
This type shall contain the available OEM-specific actions for this resource.
A condition to trigger the policy or a parent condition.
This type shall contain properties that describe conditions for a policy.
The type of this condition.
This property shall contain the type of this condition.
The comparison operator for this condition, if applicable.
This property shall contain the comparison operator for condition types that require comparisons.
The value to compare against.
This property shall contain the value for the comparison operator to compare against for conditions with an operator.
The resource from which to obtain data.

This property shall contain the URI to a Redfish resource from which to obtain data. If the resource is of type `Sensor` and the `Property` is not present, the `Reading` property from the `Sensor` reading shall be used.
The property path in the resource from which to obtain data.
This property shall contain the property path from which to obtain data. The value shall follow RFC6901-defined JSON pointer notation rules.
Subordinate conditions that are evaluated to determine the status of this condition.
This property shall contain an array of subordinate conditions that are evaluated to determine the status of this condition.
A response that is executed in the order specified.
This type shall contain properties that describe response to a policy.
The action type of this response.
This property shall contain the action type of this response.
The URI on which to perform the response action.
This property shall contain the URI on which to perform the response action.
The delay in seconds before performing the response action.
This property shall contain the number of seconds to wait before performing the response action.
The type of reset to perform if the action type is `Reset`.
This property shall contain the type of reset to perform if `ResponseAction` contains `Reset`. If `ResponseAction` does not contain `Reset`, this property shall be ignored.
The event parameters for a response if the action type is `Event`.
This property shall contain the event parameters for a response if `ResponseAction` contains `Event`. If `ResponseAction` does not contain `Event`, this property shall be ignored.
The HTTP/HTTPS parameters for a response if the action type is `HTTP`.
This property shall contain the HTTP/HTTPS parameters for a response if `ResponseAction` contains `HTTP`. If `ResponseAction` does not contain `HTTP`, this property shall be ignored.
The OEM extension property.
This property shall contain the OEM extensions. All values for properties contained in this object shall conform to the Redfish Specification-described requirements.
Parameters for an event response type.
This type shall contain properties that describe the event to send as a response.
The identifier of the message to send in the event.

This property shall contain the identifier of the message to send as the `MessageId` property in the event. If the value is in the `MessageRegistryPrefix.MessageKey` format, the service shall use the highest version of the message supported by the service. If the value is in the `MessageRegistryPrefix.MajorVersion.MinorVersion.MessageKey` format, the service shall use the exact value in the event response.
The origin of condition to send in the event.

This property shall contain the origin of condition to send as the `OriginOfCondition` property in the event. If this property is not specified or is an empty string, the origin of condition shall be the URI of this policy.
The message arguments to send in the event.
This property shall contain the message arguments to send as the `MessageArgs` property in the event.
Parameters for an HTTP/HTTPS response type.
This type shall contain properties that describe the HTTP/HTTPS operation to perform as a response.
The type of HTTP operation to perform.
This property shall contain the type of HTTP operation to perform.
The HTTP headers to include when performing the HTTP operation.
This property shall contain an object consisting of the names and values of HTTP headers to include when performing the HTTP operation. This property shall be an empty object in responses.
The body of the HTTP operation to perform.
This property shall contain the body of HTTP/HTTPS operation to send.
The HTTP header value is the property value. The header name is the property name.
This type shall contain the HTTP header name and value to include when performing an HTTP operation for a policy response.
Check whether the values to compare are equal.
This value shall indicate that the condition evaluates to true if the value calculated exactly matches the value specified by the condition.
Check whether the values to compare not equal.
This value shall indicate that the condition evaluates to true if the value calculated does not match the value specified by the condition.
Check whether the value calculated is greater than the value specified in the condition.

This value shall indicate that the condition evaluates to true if the value calculated is greater than the value specified by the condition. If both values evaluate to numbers, the service shall perform numeric comparison. Otherwise, the service shall perform string comparison.
Check whether the value calculated is less than the value specified in the condition.

This value shall indicate that the condition evaluates to true if the value calculated is less than the value specified by the condition. If both values evaluate to numbers, the service shall perform numeric comparison. Otherwise, the service shall perform string comparison.
Check whether the value calculated is greater than or equal to the value specified in the condition.

This value shall indicate that the condition evaluates to true if the value calculated is greater than or equal to the value specified by the condition. If both values evaluate to numbers, the service shall perform numeric comparison. Otherwise, the service shall perform string comparison.
Check whether the value calculated is less than or equal to the value specified in the condition.

This value shall indicate that the condition evaluates to true if the value calculated is less than or equal to the value specified by the condition. If both values evaluate to numbers, the service shall perform numeric comparison. Otherwise, the service shall perform string comparison.
The response performs an HTTP `GET` operation.
This value shall indicate that the response sends an HTTP `GET` operation as specified in RFC2616.
The response performs an HTTP `PATCH` operation.
This value shall indicate that the response sends an HTTP `PATCH` operation as specified in RFC2616.
The response performs an HTTP `POST` operation.
This value shall indicate that the response sends an HTTP `POST` operation as specified in RFC2616.
The response performs an HTTP `DELETE` operation.
This value shall indicate that the response sends an HTTP `DELETE` operation as specified in RFC2616.
